guidelineStrength: Mixed GRADE strengths; examples are reported individually in findings. A strong recommendation does not imply high-certainty evidence.
title: Surviving Sepsis Campaign: international guidelines for management of sepsis and septic shock 2026
shortTitle: SSC 2026 adults: immediate treatment, repeated reassessment and conditional fluid targets
summary: The adult update provides 129 statements, including 46 new statements. For ED care, it retains rapid antibiotics for shock or probable/definite sepsis, permits rapid investigation for possible sepsis without shock, and frames initial fluids as a conditional recommendation requiring repeated reassessment.
whyItMatters: Distinguish possible infection without shock from high-likelihood sepsis and shock when setting antibiotic urgency. Do not delay necessary vasopressors solely for central access.
limitations: Several immediately relevant recommendations rest on low or very-low-certainty evidence. Fixed fluid volumes and MAP targets require clinical context; later 2026 trials were not necessarily incorporated.
population: Adults with sepsis or septic shock, including immediate prehospital and hospital care.
intervention: Updated screening, antimicrobials and hemodynamic management recommendations.
primaryEndpoint: GRADE-based recommendations rather than one trial outcome.
findings: For sepsis-induced hypoperfusion or septic shock, at least 30 mL/kg IV crystalloid within three hours is conditional, with low-certainty evidence and ongoing reassessment.
An initial MAP target of 65 mm Hg is strong with moderate-certainty evidence.
Peripheral initiation of vasopressors rather than waiting for central access is conditional, with very-low-certainty evidence.
evidenceNotes: Current SCCM recommendation table reviewed. Springer verifies March 23 online date; May is the print issue. The May 5 correction (10.1007/s00134-026-08410-9) concerns four author names with stray trailing letters, according to the public correction abstract at https://researchinformation.umcutrecht.nl/en/publications/publisher-correction-surviving-sepsis-campaign-international-guid/ . No clinical recommendation changes are stated there. Complete guideline and subscription-only correction PDF were not reviewed.
